newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha cash holds steady as crack blows out.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha cash holds steady as crack blows out.

text.p: NWE naphtha cash prices held steady on Thursday as traders bid up the prompt market and bucked the sharp selloff in crude oil futures.
As a result, the crack spread widened out to levels that both traders and end-users agreed were not fundamentally justified, and maybe not sustainable.

But naphtha swaps did fall sharply on the back of crude oil futures, which touched their lowest levels since the middle of September, and brokers said their was heavy swaps trading, including against other products.
Feb swaps ended $4.50 lower at $223.50/$224.50 a tonne and March fell $5.50 to $214.50/$215.50. April also lost $5.50 to finish at $208.50/$209.50.
Physical cargoes were roughly unchanged near $230 cif, however.
A 25,000 tonne cargo of pipeline spec material, plus or minus 10,000 tonnes, traded at $230 cif NWE for delivery by the end of the month, one source said.

"There is not any physical trading apart from what the traders are doing," he said. "The numbers are so high and the cracks are so high, the end-users are not going to do anything and will sit on the sidelines...They are incredulous."
"And it's going to get worse as crude comes down. The cracks are out of sync," he said.
Using a simple crack spread of March Brent futures to Feb naphtha, the spread is a whopping $66, compared to what some traders normally considering a rich level of $50, he said.
